name: Low-Speed Electric Bicycle
description: A bicycle with fully operable pedals and an electric motor of less than 750 watts, in one of three classes: Class 1 and Class 3 pedal-assist up to 20 and 28 mph, and Class 2 motor-propelled up to 20 mph. Defined by Illinois Vehicle Code §1-140.10 (625 ILCS 5/1-140.10) and regulated by §11-1517; SB 3484 (Public Act 104-0854) amends both effective January 1, 2027.

restrictions.rule: A bicycle with fully operable pedals and a motor of less than 750 watts
Class 1 assists only while the rider pedals and stops at 20 mph; Class 2's motor can propel it alone, up to 20 mph; Class 3 assists only while pedaling and stops at 28 mph
Class 2's motor must cut out when the brakes are applied; Class 1 and Class 3 motors must cut out when the rider stops pedaling
Class 3 must have a speedometer showing its speed in miles per hour
Meets the CPSC's bicycle requirements (16 CFR part 1512)

Carries a permanent label, in at least 9-point Arial, stating its class, top assisted speed and motor wattage; no one may knowingly change its speed capability or motor engagement without replacing the label
Class 3 riders must be 16 or older; a younger passenger may ride on one designed to carry passengers
Class 1 and Class 2 riders must also be 15 or older, and a rider under 18 may carry a passenger only if the passenger is their sibling, stepsibling, child or stepchild
Follows the bicycle rules of the road and may be ridden on any road open to bicycles, including bike lanes
May not be ridden on a sidewalk
Allowed on bicycle paths unless the municipality, county or local authority in charge bans it or a class of it
Allowed on bicycle paths unless the state agency in charge, the Department of Natural Resources on its land, or a park, forest preserve, conservation or transit district restricts it
Local authorities may regulate it, including requiring local registration and licensing
No other unit of local government, home-rule units included, may regulate it
Not a motor vehicle, moped or motor driven cycle: no driver's license, title or state registration
An electric bicycle that doesn't meet this definition is a motor driven cycle, which needs a driver's license and is barred from sidewalks, bike lanes, bicycle paths and bike trails
